verdicts.quote: “This API implementation adheres to RFC 6749 - The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework… [for] user_access_token.”
verdicts.reason: Lark’s user-scoped access uses OAuth 2.0; that’s the primary method an agent would use to act on a user’s account across tenants.

verdicts.quote: “must first pass the ISV certification… Marketplace applications need to be strictly audited by Lark’s official operations.”
verdicts.reason: Devs can self-serve apps, but public distribution (store apps) requires ISV certification and platform review, fitting “app_review.”

verdicts.quote: “providing a rich set of OpenAPI tools that cover Lark's core functions (such as messages, groups, calendars, Base apps, etc.).”
verdicts.reason: Vendor docs indicate APIs span multiple major product areas (IM, groups, calendar, Base/bitable, etc.), consistent with “broad.”

verdicts.quote: “This is the Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool…”
verdicts.reason: The MCP server is published and maintained under Lark’s official GitHub org, so classification is “official.”

verdicts.quote: “Starter | … basic API calls… limited to 10,000 times per month… There are currently no restrictions on store apps calling APIs.”
verdicts.reason: It’s buildable now with self-serve creds, but caveats include app review for store apps and plan-based rate limits for custom apps—hence “ready_with_caveats.”
